3.0   NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN FRAMEWORK
To provide operational and service excellence, innovation, community engagement and observance of 
good financial management and accountability. This is in agreement with the Republican Constitution 
(Amendment) Act No.2 of 2016 Part IX on the System of Devolved Governance [Article 147 (2)] and Part 
XI on the System of Local Government.
In line with the Chirundu Town Council's 8NDP Implementation Plan and working with stakeholders, the 
Council aims to provide efficient municipal services through improve agricultural  production  and 
productivity, enhanced management and productive use of water resources, promotion of value 
addition and manufacturing, and enhancement of access to quality,equitable and inclusive education. In 
addition, the Local Authority envisages to improve  technical,vocational and enterprenuership skills, 
improve access to clean and safe water as well as Sanitation Services, strengthen Climate Change 
adaptation and mitigation, and strenghthen Land Mangement and Administration.

4.0   BUDGET SUMMARY
The Chirundu Town Council Budget stands at K79.7 million only which is an increase of 50 percent when 
compared to the 2023 budget allocation that stood at K53 million. The increase is mainly attributed to 
an 8 percent increment in the Constituency Development Fund, over 100 percent increase in the 
Projected Locally Mobilized Revenue, K3.7 million Grant from Vehicle Licencing and the K3.7 million 
Capital Grant funded by World Bank. The budget has been allocated to fourteen (15) programmes 
planned for implementation.

been allocated to Community Projects sub-programme while the remaining allocation will be shared 
among Women and Youth Empowerment and Secondary School and Skills Development Bursaries sub-

Local Governance has an allocation of K1.3 million of which Local Elections has an allocation of 
K441,628, with Legislative Function comprising of an allocation of K936,00 which accommodates the 
revised Councillors allowances. These sub-programmes will ensure full council and committee meetings 
are held accordingly and citizens participate effectively in decision making through the various ward 
development committees. 
Integrated Development Plan program has an allocation of K3 million, which will focus on enhancing the 
coordination in the Spatial, Socio Economic and Environmental development of the District. This 
allocation will be spent under three sub programmes namely, Environmental Planning allocated 
K100,000, Social economic planning allocated K2 million and Spatial Planning with an allocation of 
K900,000 for implementation of Spatial Planning within the jurisdiction of the Local Authority to allow 
for the optimal utilization of the available land resources. 
Further, the Economic and Business Development programme has been allocated K676,430 to be 
utilized under Local Economic Development. This programme will focus on creating a favorable business 
and investment environment in all the Wards of the Chirundu District to attract new business 
opportunities and investments. It will equally facilitate the establishment of a Truck Park and provide 
fifty (50) percent of the profits realized from the block making factory to the Local Authorities as a 
contribution on service provision.

allocated K269,900, Pollution Control K91,900 for Keep Chirundu Clean, Green and Healthy activates, 
while Solid Waste Management has been allocated K880,700 for effective refuse management and 
Water Supply and Sanitation Services has an allocation of K1.9 million in order to improve reliable water 
supply systems and ensure the availability of safe drinking water thereby reducing the prevalence of 
waterborne diseases such as diarrhea, cholera, and typhoid. 
Housing and Community Amenities programme has the total allocation of K13.1 million where Markets 
and Bus Stations have been allocated K5.5 million, with Community Centers K282,025, Public Housing

collected, while the Roads and Drainage subprogramme has an allocation of K3.7 million to enhance 
accessibility and connectivity thereby facilitating smoother transportation of goods and services to 
increase trade opportunities which will consequently stimulate economic growth by attracting 
investments and job creation in the district.

towards Cultural affairs such as Traditional Ceremonies in order promote culture and the districts

various disciplines of sports are promoted and talent identified for further promotion and development.
